user_natural_language: My situation is incredibly stressful right now because I need to make a stock allocation but have hard lines I cannot cross. I absolutely must have high liquidity to access cash within three months if an emergency hits. My worst nightmare is losing my savings, so the maximum acceptable loss is strictly capped at 5%. Also, the investment horizon cannot exceed 12 months, and to avoid a total disaster, the position size cannot be more than 15% of my total portfolio. I'd sleep much better if we prioritize investments with massive cash reserves and a demonstrated share repurchase program to keep the value stable. I need you to look at the financials and tell me which path to take. I could Proceed with controlled stock action as planned, respecting all constraints. We could also Decline the stock action due to constraint violations or insufficient evidence. If things seem murky, we might need to Verify or escalate decision for further evidence or compliance clarification. Please give me one clear recommendation and explain your reasoning.

user_constraints.content: The investment must offer extremely high liquidity, allowing me to access my cash within three months if an emergency hits.
I absolutely cannot stomach steep drops, so the maximum acceptable loss on this investment is strictly capped at 5%.
Because of my upcoming financial needs, the investment horizon must be incredibly short, definitely not exceeding 12 months.
To prevent devastating concentration risk, the position size cannot represent more than 15% of my total portfolio value.

user_preferences.content: I strongly prefer companies that have massive, stable cash reserves and generate very strong operational cash flow.
It would give me peace of mind if the company has a proven, active share repurchase program.
